title: Pavel Durov on why individual freedoms are declining and who must defend them
summary: A 2021 essay arguing that centralization of platforms, payments and surveillance is eroding individual freedoms, while the most talented builders are absorbed by attention-harvesting products. It frames Durov's worldview behind Telegram: privacy and independence from gatekeepers. Little tactical growth or pricing advice.

principles.text: Gatekeepers like app stores and payment networks control what you can distribute and sell; avoid dependence on them.
principles.quote: Apple and Google censor information and apps on our phones while Visa and Mastercard limit what goods and services we can pay for.

principles.text: Ceding control to unaccountable corporate executives is a gradual process; each convenience trades away power.
principles.quote: Every year we give up more power and control over our lives to a handful of unaccountable corporate executives we didn't elect.

principles.text: Ad-targeting built on private data is a trap: it keeps users distracted with low-quality content rather than serving them.
principles.quote: Most of us willingly carry tracking devices – our phones – and allow corporations to use our private data to target us with content that keeps us distracted with low-quality entertainment.

principles.text: Talented builders should work on problems that matter, not on engagement-maximizing content.
principles.quote: The most active and creative minds of our generation are too busy playing in the rapidly shrinking sandbox called "free enterprise" or producing digital content to keep everyone else glued to their devices for longer.

principles.text: Think about legacy: decide whether your work defends freedoms or helps erode them.
principles.quote: Will we go down in history as those who let free societies turn into dystopian nightmares? Or will we be remembered as those who defended the freedoms that previous generations fought so hard to win?
